label: first copy step echoing an initial i/u, in short w-containing sequences
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (~0.003% of steps). About 68% of activation mass is at the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx==1), where the input is the fed-back first original token. Nearly all of these have first token i (about 58% of mass) or u (about 35%), and the sequence usually contains w, often at positions 1-3 (e.g. i w w <DEL> [i]). The strongest activations are in short sequences (L=3-4) that start with i and contain w. The other ~30% of mass is scattered across original-phase steps (t=4-7) in u/i-initial sequences rich in w/z (e.g. u t w z w [1]), and that part has no clean predicate. It never fires at t<4 or on the delimiter, and almost never at later copy steps. Precision is very low: most i/u-echo steps with w do not fire, so the feature looks like a sharp conjunction this predicate does not fully capture. The recorded predicate (i echo, L<=4, w present) gets the best dev F1, about 0.24; the broader version (i or u echo, w present) covers about 60% of mass at about 2% precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=u (+3.77), L=3 & recall_idx=1 (+2.75), orig3=w (+2.34), orig0=i (+2.21), orig1=w (+2.17), orig4=w (+2.14). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-2.08), prev3_tok=- (-1.71), prev3_tok=u (-1.43), to_go=4 (-0.76).
